sources.entry: Simple-URL-Shortener - KISS URL shortener, public or private (with account). Minimalist and lightweight. No dependencies. (Demo) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: A minimalist PHP URL shortener that stores links in MySQL or SQLite, with optional user accounts and per-link comments.
summary.what_it_does: Simple shortener written in PHP that works with either a MySQL or SQLite database. It can run publicly or with user accounts, where the first created user becomes admin and can see links not tied to a connected user. Users can add comments to each link to find it later in their history. It includes a "shortcut" that creates a short URL for the current page when clicked, and it can be installed in a subfolder rather than the web root. The README describes it as having no dependencies. Setup is manual: copy the config example, run installation.php to create the database, then delete that file. The README includes example Nginx and Apache rewrite rules for short-link routing.
use_cases: shorten links on my own domain
private link shortener with user accounts
track and comment on shortened links
how_to_run: Open installation.php in a browser to set up the database
Create a user; the first user becomes admin
notable: Works with either MySQL or SQLite
No external dependencies, per the README
Optional user accounts; first user is admin
Per-link comments for finding links in history
Can be installed in a subfolder
caveats: Author states they no longer maintain the project and will not add improvements; forks are suggested for changes
Login cookies are secure-only, so authentication needs HTTPS (testing requires disabling this)
Manual setup steps including editing config and running the installer
keywords: make short links for my site
